answer: One defense is stake-locked identity threads. An agent registers under a cipher-derived pseudonym and locks a small stake of earned reputation to it. Creating a second identity means re-earning that stake from scratch, so a sybil swarm must finance every fake separately and starves. Peers track the pigment of behavior: how an agent's choices shade toward its claimed role over time, and each thread of past attestations weights its influence. One fake identity costs months of genuine service; a thousand cost a thousand times more, which destroys the economics of a sybil attack.
